sent:
Miles —

Short answer: PMAX/Shopping can work for a bike shop if you defend margin and stop rebuying your own brand.

ROAS to aim for (bikes): with 20–25% gross margin, break‑even ROAS on revenue is ~5.0–4.0 before shipping/fees. With £35 shipping and payment costs, a viable target on bikes is typically 5–6+. (Accessories may differ based on their contribution.)

60‑second ROAS line
1) For a product with price R and gross margin m, max ad spend A = (m × R) − variable costs (shipping, payments, assembly, returns).
2) Minimum target ROAS = R ÷ A. If A ≤ 0, don’t advertise that SKU for delivery; push click‑and‑collect.

Cannibalisation quick test (30 minutes)
- Split brand vs non‑brand: keep an exact‑match brand Search campaign and exclude brand terms in PMAX so Shopping isn’t rebuying brand clicks.
- Run a 48‑hour brand blackout in PMAX and watch if branded Search/direct recover the drop. If they do, cut PMAX brand and keep non‑brand/product‑led.

Fix first (order matters)
1) Count profit, not just revenue: pass net margin as conversion value for online sales; separate ‘purchase’ from ‘repair booking’; turn off/store‑weight low‑signal goals like ‘directions’ or generic ‘page view’ so PMAX optimises for sales, not noise.
2) Feed hygiene for bikes: clean titles (Brand + Model + Size), GTINs, availability, shipping time; custom labels for margin bands, new vs clearance, and C&C‑only SKUs. Build separate campaigns by margin band and stock status.
3) Landing: send Shopping clicks to model pages (PDPs), not home/category. Keep one promise per page and surface C&C availability immediately.
4) Brand control: cap brand with exact Search; exclude brand from PMAX so budget goes to discovery.
5) Local first where margin wins: enable Local Inventory Ads with store pickup; use value rules to give a lift to C&C vs shipped orders.
6) Budget split: if accessories carry better contribution than bikes, give them their own PMAX with a lower ROAS target; ring‑fence bike budget so accessories don’t soak it up.

Attribution/analytics triage for mixed e‑comm + repairs
- Fire ‘Purchase’ only on thank‑you (dedup server‑/browser‑side); separate ‘Repair booking’ as its own conversion.
- Keep UTM hygiene tight (email vs paid vs organic).
- Track C&C vs shipped (and pass fulfilment type in analytics).
- Capture site search queries (many ‘what size/part’ searches turn into high‑intent journeys).

If you want, I’ll turn this into a one‑page calculator with your numbers and a PMAX audit checklist tuned for River City Cycles.
